recentItems.title: Africa Credit Rating Agency launched in Mauritius
recentItems.description:
The Africa Credit Rating Agency has been launched in Mauritius, where it will have its offices. The launch was attended by both AU and UN representatives. The UN Economic Commission has hailed the launch as a milestone for the African Continent. UNECA Chief Economist Hanan Morsy spoke to the SABC about the importance of the Africa Credit Rating Agency.

recentItems.title: Scores of women working on farms are marching through the streets of Cape Town
recentItems.description:
Scores of women working on farms are marching through the streets of Cape Town CBD to hand over a memorandum of demands to Parliament. 

The women are calling for improved conditions on farms, as well as labour rights and benefits. This week, women working on farms across the country gathered in the city to discuss issues affecting them. 

This includes job security, the national minimum wage, basic human rights, as well as the right to land. Rights such as sick leave and labour rights are also of major concern to them. 

They are expected to hand over their memorandum to the offices of the Department of Employment and Labour later this afternoon.

recentItems.title: Asylum seekers flock to Gqeberha refugee offices
recentItems.description:
Snaking queues were seen seen outside Home Affairs offices in Gqeberha, in the Eastern Cape. 
This as asylum seekers respond to a Constitutional Court judgment, which states - in part - that a person cannot be denied access to the asylum application process simply because they entered South Africa illegally. 

Let's bring in SABC News reporter, Nandipha Plaatjie.
